dedupe_keys.name: openlandmap soildb open compendium of soil samples and observations

description: OpenLandMap SoilDB is an open compendium of soil samples and observations that imports hundreds of soil profile and point datasets into a common structure, covering chemical and physical properties, hydraulic functions and soil spectra. Examples on the dataset list include the European LUCAS soil surveys with over 21,000 locations, the Africa Soil Profiles Database with about 15,600, SISLAC for Latin America with about 14,600 and the US NCSS characterisation data with about 19,860. It is compiled by the OpenGeoHub Foundation, which documents each import and version on GitLab. Coverage is global, continental, regional and national, as point data. Source data come as CSV files, shapefiles and databases from direct downloads and repositories such as Zenodo and Harvard Dataverse, free, each under its own open licence, such as CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0 or ODbL. Caveats: sources differ in methods, depths and dates, so harmonised values carry uncertainty, and share-alike licences apply to some combined data. For simulation it supplies soil observations to train or check soil maps used in crop, flood, drought and geotechnical models, and to parameterise ground conditions in data-poor regions. It is related to the NCSS Soil Characterization Database and Harmonized World Soil Database records in this catalogue.
